Holy cow...great work, op! And op's family! A job like that family room certainly needs all the help it can get! I like the closet and pantry removal the most....really made those spaces. So I lost track...how long was the entire family room project? It takes us months just to do one room, without flooring. :)

Tip for your next drywall project...my husband bought a sander that attaches to our shopvac. It saves a lot of cleanup. It's not perfect, but certainly is better.

Almost a year and a half from the start to finish for two rooms.

We started tearing out subfloor May 2013, I did the bedroom subfloor in august 2013, and we hit a snag. The whole project went on hold until I could find an acceptable hardwood match. I did some small projects around the house in the interim, and in December 2013 we got the wood and were able to patch the bedroom floor.

We then had to wait to sand until it got warm enough to open windows, so we sanded, stained and sealed the bedroom floor in March / April 2014, we also redid the closets at this time. Once everything was dry we moved the furniture back into the bedroom and cleared out the greatroom (we had been using it as a makeshift bedroom the entire time the bedroom was down).

In June 2014 we were ready to re-tackle the great room, but I decided that I needed to remove the closet first, and then the removing useless bits snowballed. By July 2014 we were finally ready to sand, stain and seal the floors. We also decided to redo the ceiling, in retrospect i wish I would have done the ceiling before the floor, but we weren't sure we wanted to do it. By the time we fished the ceiling and patching the walls, it was the end of August 2014. September 2014 is when we painted the greatroom, we also replaced the bathtub (not shown) and started the wood stove installation during this time. By December 2014 the woodstove was installed and ready for use.
I'm working on reclaiming a bit of dead space from a wall for a new small canned good /spice cabinet, I hope to be able to post that soon.

I work in medical IT, and while I have done some programming in the past, I would never consider myself a real programmer.
A better explanation would be that I can eventually bang out something that does the job I'm looking to have done, but it usually isn't pretty (or stable, or flexible). AutoIt has been amazing for me in that regard, as the documentation, libraries, and built in commands, combined with the free tools for developing and deploying scripts and programs are all fantastic. I've had far better luck getting things accomplished with AutoIt than other scripting languages, such as vb or powershell. So far I've written a few tools that get used in my department, in addition to other minute, or still in progress scripts... A quick launcher program that remotes to other pc's or launches (and logs into) the various programs used repeatedly in the job.
A simple script that automatically renames the sheets in any excel file to a preset name (for consistency for processing by another task). A (only slightly) more complex script that emails out any files in a specified folder at the end of one process, and moves them to an archive.

None of them are particularly brilliant or novel scripts, but they save me time on a daily basis, and improve consistency and stability with various tasks.

I would love to hear what other clever scripts, or even impressive large scale programs, people have built using AutoIt.
AutoIt is a godsend for the novice programmer.
